review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new definition is `paperLowLevelMaximal`, a supremum over nonzero modulations of the enorm of a Bochner integral against the project-specific kernel `paperLowCZKernel`. Mathlib has no maximal-operator concept of this kind. The definition is built from `iSup`, `enorm` and `integral`, and it is used in PositiveLowFullEndpoint and PositiveLowFullHeightIdentity. A close sibling, `paperLowBadAtomMaximal` in LowKernelRealMaximal.lean, differs on purpose: it integrates over `centeredInterval` and uses `ENNReal.ofReal ‖…‖`. That sibling sits in the same project, not in Mathlib, so I did not count it. The other declarations are theorems, which the rubric excludes. I found no competing duplicate of a Mathlib concept. I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for related maximal functions, but nothing in the file suggests one.
